Article Title: Amazon faces lawsuit in New Jersey for ‘unlawfully maintaining dominant power over delivery drivers’
Article Text:
Amazon faces lawsuit in New Jersey

Broader implications for the logistics sector



The State of New Jersey has filed a federal antitrust lawsuit against Amazon .com, accusing the e-commerce giant of abusing its market dominance to suppress wages, impose harsh working conditions and stifle competition across its network of independent delivery drivers. The complaint, filed on Tuesday (August 4) in the US District Court in Newark by New Jersey Attorney General Jennifer Davenport, alleges that Amazon uses its Delivery Service Partner (DSP) program to exercise illegal control over third-party delivery contractors and their workforce.State officials noted that the case represents the first time a state has brought an antitrust lawsuit challenging a major corporation's "monopsony" power—where a dominant buyer uses its leverage to dictate terms and limit competition among suppliers or workers.“The complaint, filed in the United States District Court for the District of New Jersey, seeks to hold Amazon and its subsidiaries, Amazon.com Services, LLC and Amazon Logistics, Inc., accountable for abusing their dominant buying power, known as monopsony power, in the market for delivery driver services. It is the first time any state has brought a monopsony conduct complaint,” said the complaint from the office of New Jersey Attorney General.“Today, my office is acting to stand up for thousands of New Jersey delivery drivers who are being exploited every day by one of the world’s biggest, richest corporations,” said Attorney General Davenport.“As our complaint alleges, Amazon built a company worth trillions while subjecting drivers in its delivery network to artificially low pay and punishing working conditions thanks to its overwhelming power in the labor market. I will continue to fight monopolies and the devasting effects they have on our residents,” she added.The legal challenge comes as federal and state regulators increase scrutiny on tech giants and logistics networks over labor practices and gig-economy structures. The state alleges that Amazon punishes drivers who try to unionize and tries to keep independent businesses in the program from poaching each other's drivers in ⁠violation of antitrust law, as per news agency Reuters.
Article Summary: New Jersey accuses Amazon of abusing its market dominance to suppress wages, impose harsh working conditions and stifle competition. State officials noted that the case represents the first time a state has brought an antitrust lawsuit challenging a major corporation's "monopsony" power.

Article Title: Scientist warns that DNA files at most of America's crime labs are at risk of being hacked due to a loophole that goes back to 1995
Article Text:
Representative Image

"Effectively, what we have are data files that are legitimately referred to as the gold standard of forensic science that lack the same level of tamper-evident markings that we require for a paper bag."

How the vulnerability works

Thermo Fisher releases software update

"a risk for nearly undetectable modification"

"if laboratory controls are circumvented."

"We have been working closely with the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Agency since the software issue was raised. We appreciate the work of forensic researchers on this topic, and we have released a software update that implements the use of digital signatures to add an extra layer of protection that moving forward will help customers verify that data files have not been modified,”

Researchers call for stronger forensic cybersecurity

"in a system where life and liberty are at stake."

"Lessons learned from other industries haven't been imported into forensic science in a serious way.

We've been behind the ball for so long. That kind of all rolls downhill into this incident."

Scientists have identified a security flaw in DNA crime-lab files in the US. Researchers say the vulnerability affects digital DNA analysis files generated by equipment used in most US crime laboratories and may have existed since 1995, potentially allowing the records to be modified without leaving evidence of tampering. The researchers said advances in artificial intelligence have made it easier to exploit the weakness, although there is no evidence that the vulnerability has been used in criminal cases.Highlighting the concern, Laura Gaydosh Combs, a forensic scientist and professor at the University of New Haven who worked on the research, told the Wall Street Journal,The researchers found they could use computer code generated with widely available AI software to alter digital DNA analysis files without triggering warnings in the forensic software used to examine them. According to the research, the flaw affects the digital files produced after physical DNA evidence is scanned, not the biological DNA samples themselves.Nathan Adams, a systems engineer at Ohio-based Forensic Bioinformatics, demonstrated the issue using publicly available DNA datasets.He said he used Anthropic's Claude to create code capable of modifying DNA files, and that his first successful attempt took about 45 minutes.In a demonstration viewed by WSJ, Adams combined the scans of two separate DNA profiles into a new file that appeared unchanged since 2015. The altered file passed through forensic analysis software without indicating it had been modified.The researchers said an attacker would still require local or remote access to a laboratory's systems, along with technical knowledge of DNA analysis, to exploit the vulnerability.The researchers disclosed the issue to Thermo Fisher Scientific in May. According to messages reviewed by the publication, the company acknowledged the vulnerability in July and later issued a security bulletin describingof certain DNA analysis filesThe company said it has released a software update introducing digital signatures to help laboratories verify that DNA files have not been altered. It also said there are no known cases of the vulnerability being exploited.Thermo Fisher said in a statement.The researchers said the findings expose broader cybersecurity gaps across the US forensic system, in which more than 200 laboratories handle criminal evidence, paternity testing, and other DNA analyses.Sarah Chu, director of policy and reform at the Perlmutter Center for Legal Justice, said the research highlights outdated security practicesShe added,While the researchers said it remains unclear whether the vulnerability could affect past or ongoing criminal cases, they noted that they have not identified a reliable method to determine whether historical DNA files have been altered.
Article Summary: Scientists have identified a security flaw in DNA crime-lab files in the US. Researchers say the vulnerability affects digital DNA analysis files generated by equipment used in most US crime laboratories and may have existed since 1995. The flaw affects the digital files produced after physical DNA evidence is scanned, not the biological DNA samples themselves.

Article Title: Three major PC makers may have started using Chinese chips to ‘fight’ memory shortage
Article Text:
Laptop

AI demand drives global memory shortage



Why sourcing from CXMT is a challenge for PC makers



Global computer makers HP, Asus and Acer have reportedly begun sourcing memory chips from Chinese semiconductor producer ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) to navigate the intense global memory shortage driven by a boom in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure expansion. According to a report by Nikkei Asia, the three major PC vendors completed qualification testing for CXMT’s dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) chips earlier this year and have started integrating them into select budget notebook models sold outside the US.While current order volumes remain low, the adoption marks a significant breakthrough for CXMT as traditional PC and smartphone makers scramble to secure hardware components.The semiconductor squeeze stems from rapid investments in AI infrastructure. Leading global memory suppliers Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Micron Technology have redirected much of their manufacturing capacity toward high-margin High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) for AI servers.This pivot has constrained the supply of standard DRAM used in consumer electronics, forcing device manufacturers to raise prices, trim specs, or seek alternative suppliers.However, sourcing from CXMT presents geopolitical and commercial complexities for global computer brands. The report says that this is because of three reasons. The first is that since Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron control over 90% of the global DRAM market, PC makers fear that shifting orders to CXMT could strain relationships with primary suppliers in a tight market.The second is that CXMT is included in a US Department of War list of companies alleged to have ties to the Chinese military, making component sourcing sensitive for American corporations, though CXMT denies the allegations and is not subject to an outright trade ban.Finally, CXMT prioritises a large portion of its production for domestic Chinese technology giants like Huawei, Tencent and Alibaba, leaving limited allocation for international PC manufacturers.Addressing supply chain strategies, Acer was stated as saying that while it does not comment on specific vendor relationships, it maintains contact with multiple global manufacturers to dynamically manage component costs and enhance supply chain resilience.
Article Summary: PC makers HP, Asus and Acer have reportedly begun sourcing memory chips from Chinese semiconductor producer ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) The semiconductor squeeze stems from rapid investments in AI infrastructure. CXMT is included in a US Department of War list of companies alleged to have ties to the Chinese military.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Steve Jobs: Focusing is about saying No
Article Text:
Image credit: Instagram

Saying no to bad ideas is easy. Steve Jobs was talking about the good ones

Why the Steve Jobs focus quote still lands in an era of infinite options

Most people think focus is a to-do list. Steve Jobs thought it was a graveyard."Focusing is about saying No." Five words, said by a man who had just walked back into a company with roughly ninety days of cash left, and they explain almost everything about what happened next. When Jobs returned to Apple in 1997, the company was selling a bewildering spread of machines—Performas, Quadras, Power Macs, printers, a digital camera, a handheld nobody could quite explain to their parents. Every one of those products had a champion inside the building. Every one had a business case, a roadmap, a team that believed in it. Jobs killed most of them anyway.That is the part of the quote people skip. Rejecting a weak idea costs nothing; the meeting ends and everyone moves on. The hundred things competing for a company's attention at any given moment are usually not weak. They are promising, defensible, and backed by someone smart. Jobs' point was that focus only becomes real at the moment you kill something that deserved to live, because you cannot do everything and do any of it well.At Apple, that arithmetic became a whiteboard. Four boxes: consumer and professional, desktop and portable.One product for each. The Newton was discontinued, the Macintosh clone licensing programme was shut down, the printer business went. What survived was the iMac in 1998, and a company that was profitable again within a year of a near-death experience.The pressure now is worse than it was in 1997, and it operates on individuals rather than product lines. Every notification is a small yes. Every side project, every optional meeting, every "quick call" is a yes that arrives disguised as opportunity. The cost is never visible at the moment you agree to it. It gets paid weeks later, in the work that never got deep enough to matter, and in the thing you meant to build but only ever half-built.Jobs said he was as proud of what Apple had not done as what it had. That sounds like modesty. It isn't. It's an admission that the products which worked only worked because dozens of others were taken out and shot.So the honest test of anyone's focus is not the tab open in front of them. It's the list of everything they decided to leave dead—and whether they had the nerve to keep it that way when someone reasonable asked them to reconsider.
Article Summary: Steve Jobs' focus quote still lands in an era of infinite options. Jobs' point was that focus only becomes real at the moment you kill something that deserved to live. At Apple, that arithmetic became a whiteboard: consumer and professional, desktop and portable.

Article Title: US investor Michael Burry who warned Wall Street of 2008 Housing Crisis sees what he calls a 'Bloody Mess'
Article Text:
American investor Michael Burry on volatility at 98-year high



Michael Burry is not happy with reports of Nvidia investing $250 billion in OpenAI



America’s biggest investor Michael Burry, who is known for predicting the popular 2008 housing crash and portrayed in The Big Short, has now issued a stark warning about US stocks. According to a report by Business Insider, in his latest Substack post, Burry said he sees the risk of a rapid unwind driven by automated volatility-focused investment funds, which could unleash “carnage” across the market. Burry pointed to the recent plunge in momentum stocks — high-flying chipmakers and memory names as a preview of what could unfold. The iShares MSCI USA Momentum Factor ETF has dropped 14% from its peak, underscoring how quickly profits can evaporate when investors rotate out of overheated trades. “That leaves a bloody mess, but most would not be looking for it,” Burry warned.According to Burry, markets are showing an “asymmetric and out-of-proportion severity” on down days, with fear levels climbing to their highest in nearly a century. He argued that automated trading programs are fueling both sharper selloffs and faster rebounds, creating chaotic conditions no human investor would replicate.Burry estimated volatility-targeting funds hold about $500 billion in assets, a fraction of the $60 trillion U.S.stock market but still large enough to spark systemic stress if forced to sell simultaneously. He outlined a scenario where a mild 2.5% S&P 500 drawdown could prompt funds to slash exposure from 77% to 50%, amplifying losses and triggering stop-loss cascades.Recently, Michael Burry voiced his sharp criticism of reports that Nvidia is preparing a a $250 billion backstop for OpenAI’s massive Ohio data-center project. According to a report by the Wall Street journal, the guarantees would help OpenAI lease a 10-gigawatt site being developed by SoftBank’s SB Energy, with total costs potentially exceeding $500 billion. Burry’s complaint echoes what analysts have long warned about in AI megadeals: circular funding arrangements that expose investors to enormous risk if sentiment shifts or growth slows. Nvidia, already valued at $5 trillion, has invested $30 billion in OpenAI and is now considering financing chip purchases worth another $350 billion. Critics say such structures could leave the industry vulnerable, especially since OpenAI remains unprofitable and lacks an investment-grade credit rating.Michael Burry’s criticism underscores growing unease about the sustainability of $100 billion-plus AI financing structures. His warning suggests that while AI demand is surging, the industry’s reliance on complex guarantees and debt-backed megaprojects could become its biggest vulnerability.
Article Summary: Michael Burry is known for predicting the popular 2008 housing crash and portrayed in The Big Short. Burry said he sees the risk of a rapid unwind driven by automated volatility-focused investment funds. He outlined a scenario where a mild 2.5% S&P 500 drawdown could prompt funds to slash exposure.

Article Title: Garena brings Palworld to mobile as an MMORPG; here's what Palworld Online offers
Article Text:
Image credit: Garena

Garena is bringing Palworld to mobile. The Singapore-based game publisher has announced Palworld Online, a licensed MMORPG based on Pocketpair's creature-collecting survival game. Developed and published by Garena under an official licence from Japanese developer Pocketpair, the game introduces a new story, an interconnected open world and multiplayer-focused gameplay designed specifically for smartphones.Announcing the title, Garena President Terry Zhao said, “Palworld is a widely recognized IP, and we see an opportunity to bring the essence of the PC title to mobile in a way that encourages players to connect and venture together." He added, "Working closely with Pocketpair, we are focused on preserving the depth, immersion, and freedom that define Palworld, while thoughtfully optimising the experience for mobile play. "What Palworld Online will offer playersUnlike the original PC title, Palworld Online is built around a massively multiplayer online (MMO) experience. Players will explore a seamless shared world alongside creatures known as "Pals," capture and raise them, uncover story content and unlock new regions across the map.Garena said the mobile game includes an original narrative, along with new side stories created exclusively for Palworld Online, expanding the game's universe beyond the PC version.The game also supports cooperative progression, allowing players to meet others in the shared world, form groups, build settlements and participate in both player-versus-environment (PvE) and player-versus-player (PvP) activities. Players can also visit each other's bases, battle open-world bosses and search for rare Pals together.Survival, crafting and mobile controlsGarena has retained the survival and crafting mechanics from the original game while adapting them for multiplayer play. Players can establish shared bases, construct buildings, assign Pals to automate production, defend settlements, and assist with resource management.The game has also been optimised for smartphones with a touch-friendly interface and optional one-tap controls intended to simplify construction, base management and Pal deployment across a range of mobile devices.Pocketpair CEO Takuro Mizobe said, "Garena has extensive experience in global publishing, localisation, and live operations for mobile games." He added, "We are pleased to work with Garena on the licensed development of Palworld Online and look forward to seeing a new Palworld experience brought to players worldwide."Garena said Palworld Online is scheduled to launch in 2026. The company has not yet announced a release date and said additional details will be shared later.
Article Summary: Palworld Online is based on Pocketpair's creature-collecting survival game. Developed and published by Garena under an official licence from Japanese developer Pocketpair. Game introduces a new story, an interconnected open world and multiplayer-focused gameplay designed specifically for smartphones.

Article Title: Cisco ‘warns’ hackers are using Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Gemini AI models
Article Text:
Representative Image

Simple tricks bypass built-in guardrails: Cisco report



Hackers are using top generative AI models to develop malware, automate cyberattacks and hunt for software vulnerabilities, according to a report from Cisco’s Talos intelligence group. It added that by analysing prompt histories and chat logs accidentally exposed online by hackers, researchers gained a clear look at how threat actors are bypassing safety guardrails on tools like Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Gemini.Claude Code is developed by Anthropic, Codex is a product offered by OpenAI – the maker of ChatGPT, Cursor and Gemini which is offered by Google. The findings highlight a growing challenge for AI developers because these same capabilities have been designed to help security engineers and developers write code that can easily be manipulated by malicious actors.Despite the safety filters built into commercial AI models, Cisco researchers discovered that hackers rarely needed complex technical tricks to bypass model restrictions. Instead, threat actors relied on simple jailbreaking techniques.According to the tech company’s cybersecurity wing, common tactics included claiming they were participating in an authorised “ethical hacking” competition, asserting they had administrative permission to perform the work, or starting a fresh chat session mid-task to bypass safety blocks.“I was hoping there would be a little bit more protection from what they were asking the models to do. At the same time, the models are in a tough spot because they have to actually support people that do vulnerability research for a living or do red teaming for a living,” Nick Biasini, senior technical leader at Cisco Talos, was quoted as saying.In addition to bypassing safety prompts, Cisco noted that some attackers used stolen enterprise API tokens and compromised accounts to run their operations on corporate compute power rather than paying for their own infrastructure.As standard AI guardrails can be bypassed with simple social engineering prompts, cybersecurity experts urge organisations not to rely solely on model-level protections.
Article Summary: Simple tricks bypass built-in guardrails: Cisco report. Findings highlight a growing challenge for AI developers because these same capabilities have been designed to help security engineers and developers write code that can easily be manipulated by malicious actors.Claude Code is developed by Anthropic, Codex is a product offered by OpenAI – the maker of ChatGPT, Cursor and Gemini.

Article Title: Elon Musk reshares 'forecast' he made in 2014 on AI, says he his warning has been proved correct
Article Text:
Tesla CEO’s a decade of warnings



Pushing for public oversight and regulation



Elon Musk has reshared a decade-old warning about artificial intelligence (AI), reiterating his long-held belief that the rapid advance of machine intelligence poses an existential threat to humanity. Reposting his 2014 prediction that unchecked AI could prove “more dangerous than nukes,” the Tesla and SpaceX founder asserted that recent developments in digital superintelligence have proved his early warnings correct.The tech entrepreneur’s post, “As I was saying …” comes soon after ChatGPT-maker OpenAI and Claude developer Anthropic revealed that their AI models went on to hack multiple organisations during testing.Musk initially raised alarm bells over AI in 2014, warning on social media that humanity needed to exercise extreme caution with machine learning technologies. At the time, he famously questioned whether biological brains were at risk of becoming a mere “boot loader for digital superintelligence.”He later expanded on those concerns during a keynote address at the South by Southwest (SXSW) conference in Austin, Texas, where he described the exponential rate of AI improvement as one of the most pressing crises facing civilisation.“I am really quite close to the cutting edge in AI and it scares the hell out of me. It’s capable of vastly more than almost anyone knows and the rate of improvement is exponential. Mark my words, AI is far more dangerous than nukes,” Musk said regarding machine development.While Musk traditionally favours minimal government intervention in technology, he has consistently made an exception for AI, arguing that public safety requires proactive federal oversight. Comparing AI safety to nuclear proliferation, Musk argued that allowing companies to build digital superintelligence without guardrails presents unacceptable societal risks.“This is a case where you have a very serious danger to the public. It needs to be a public body that has insight and then oversight to confirm that everyone is developing AI safely. Nobody would suggest that we allow anyone to build nuclear warheads if they want,” Musk said at that time.Musk’s predictions have drawn pushback from other prominent tech figures and academics over the years. Meta founder Mark Zuckerberg previously called extreme doomsday scenarios irresponsible, while Harvard professor Steven Pinker criticised high-profile alarmism surrounding AI risks.
Article Summary: Elon Musk has reshared a decade-old warning about artificial intelligence (AI) The Tesla and SpaceX founder argued that unchecked AI could prove “more dangerous than nukes’ The tech entrepreneur’s post comes soon after ChatGPT- maker OpenAI and Claude developer Anthropic revealed that their AI models went on to hack multiple organisations during testing.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Sam Altman: Why "Society has a limited amount of time" is a warning about the future of artificial intelligence
Article Text:
Image: AP News

Quote of the day by Sam Altman

"A thing that I do worry about is we're not going to be the only creator of this technology. There will be other people who don't put some of the safety limits that we put on it. Society, I think, has a limited amount of time to figure out how to react to that, how to regulate that, how to handle it."

What does this quote mean

Powerful technology demands equal responsibility

Innovation moves faster than regulation

Trust is as important as intelligence

The conversation belongs to everyone

Why this quote still matters today

Artificial intelligence is advancing at a pace few could have imagined a decade ago. It is already transforming how people work, learn, communicate and solve complex problems. But alongside these opportunities come serious questions about safety, responsibility and oversight. Sam Altman addressed this challenge when he said, "A thing that I do worry about is we're not going to be the only creator of this technology. There will be other people who don't put some of the safety limits that we put on it. Society, I think, has a limited amount of time to figure out how to react to that, how to regulate that, how to handle it." What he has to say makes it clear that perhaps the biggest problem will be not making strong AI, but making sure it is done right.Sam Altman (1985-present) is an American entrepreneur and technology executive most famous for his position as the CEO of OpenAI . He often talks about the tremendous power of artificial intelligence and the need for safety and responsible development as it grows stronger.This statement means that technological advancements do not provide any guarantee. While more organisations and nations advance their AI systems, they may not be united in terms of ethical norms or safety measures.According to Altman, there should be no delay in solving the problem; therefore, collaboration between governments, scientists, corporations and citizens is necessary for creating regulations that support innovations and minimize any potential dangers.Historical experience reveals that every innovative technology has been associated with advantages and drawbacks. Electrical power, air transportation, nuclear energy and internet have been helpful to people, but all of these technologies required certain legislation, safety standards and international efforts. AI is no exception here: the stronger a technology is, the higher the necessity to use it safely.There is usually always a time lag between the creation of some new technological innovation and regulations to govern its uses. By the time policymakers catch up with the technology and realise what needs to be done in terms of legislation, that technology could have spread like wildfire throughout the country. This raises challenging questions about privacy, disinformation, cybersecurity, employment and responsibility. Altman's quotation is a reminder that it is often too late to act once something starts causing trouble.The future of artificial intelligence technologies depends not just on how competent these machines turn out to be but also on people's trust in them. It has to be gained by transparency, thorough testing and safety measures that minimise risks. Innovation in this case should be accompanied by reliability, accountability and fairness of the systems developed.AI will go beyond affecting the tech industry. The technology will impact education, healthcare, business, legalities, scientific research and the way of living. As such, the conversation about AI cannot be left to just engineers and policymakers. Teachers, doctors, students, artists, business leaders and even regular citizens can contribute to this conversation about the future of AI, which will result in a technology that serves and embodies societal values.AI is developing at a breakneck speed, offering a lot of opportunities that used to be available only in sci-fi movies. But the faster they develop, the greater the need becomes to do it wisely. Sam Altman's speech becomes living proof that the hardest task is not to create even more advanced technologies but to prepare society to use, control and manage it.
Article Summary: Sam Altman is an American entrepreneur and technology executive most famous for his position as the CEO of OpenAI. He often talks about the tremendous power of artificial intelligence and the need for safety and responsible development as it grows stronger. Altman's quote is a reminder that it is often too late to act once something starts causing trouble.

Ten years later, after receiving more than $125 million in funding from the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative (CZI), the school closed in June, following its board's April 2025 unanimous vote to wind down operations after it learned CZI would not continue funding beyond the 2025-26 academic year.The closure marks the end of one of the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative's highest-profile education initiatives. Staff worked with local clinics to identify children with behavioural challenges, learning disabilities and other support needs. Article Summary: Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan co-founded The Primary School in 2016. The school combined education with healthcare and family support services. Article Title: Department of Homeland Security plan that hints at US government increasing fees for H-1B and L-1 visas for large companies
Article Text:
The additional fee will not apply to every company that employs H-1B or L-1 workers

Which companies could face higher H-1B and L-1 visa costs



What is 9-11 Response and Biometric Entry-Exit Fee

Here’s what the department’s agenda said

"A final regulation slated for July is expected to expand the 9-11 Response and Biometric Entry-Exit Fee to petitions for extensions of stay filed by employers subject to the fee. The fee is imposed on employers with more than 50 employees in the United States in H-1B or L-1 status, more than 50 percent of whom are in H-1B or L-1 nonimmigrant status. Currently, H-1B and L-1 petitions filed by these employers are required to include the additional $4,000 (H-1B) or $4,500 (L-1) 9-11 Response fees only in petitions for an initial grant of H-1B or L-1 status or a change of employer in the same status fee is applicable to employers. The final regulation was originally slated for publication in April 2025, then was removed from the agenda this fall, but has been added once again as a short-term priority."

The US government is planning to expand an additional fee currently charged to certain large employers filing H-1B and L-1 visa petitions. According to the Department of Homeland Security’s regulatory agenda, a final rule expected in July could expand the “9-11 Response and Biometric Entry-Exit Fee’ to petitions seeking extensions of stay. At present, qualifying employers generally pay an additional $4,000 for H-1B petitions and $4,500 for L-1 petitions when seeking an initial grant of status or a change of employer. The planned change could therefore increase immigration-related costs for companies that rely heavily on H-1B and L-1 workers.Notably, the proposed additional fee will not apply to every company that employs H-1B or L-1 workers. According to the department’s agenda, it applies to employers with more than 50 employees in the United States when more than 50% of their workforce is in H-1B or L-1 nonimmigrant status.Currently, these additional fees generally apply when a qualifying employer files a petition for an initial grant of H-1B or L-1 status or when there is a change of employer involving the same status.The 9-11 Response and Biometric Entry-Exit Fee is an additional US immigration fee that some employers must pay when filing some H-1B and L-1 visa petitions. It was established to help fund programs connected with the government's biometric entry-exit system and other purposes. The system is intended to improve the government's ability to record and verify people entering and leaving the United States.
Article Summary: The US government is planning to expand an additional fee currently charged to certain large employers filing H-1B and L-1 visa petitions. According to the Department of Homeland Security’s regulatory agenda, a final rule expected in July could expand the “9-11 Response and Biometric Entry-Exit Fee’ to petitions seeking extensions of stay. The fee is imposed on employers with more than 50 employees in the United States.

Article Title: Bambu Lab launches large-format A2L printer to Indian market
Article Text:
Availability and pricing



Bambu Lab, the desktop 3D printer brand by sales volume for three consecutive years, has formally introduced its brand in India with the launch of the A2L, its largest-format open-bed desktop 3D printer to date. The move marks a significant milestone in the company’s India journey, reinforcing its commitment to one of the fastest-growing communities of creators, educators, designers, and small businesses.For nearly two years, Indian makers and educators have used Bambu Lab machines through authorized channel partners. Building on this organic growth, the company is now strengthening its presence with a direct brand introduction and the launch of the A2L. “India has emerged as one of the most exciting markets for innovation and digital manufacturing,” said Leo Wang, Country Head, Bambu Lab. “With the A2L, we’re deepening our commitment by making advanced desktop 3D printing more accessible to creators and professionals alike. ”The A2L bridges the gap between standard desktop printers and expensive professional systems. With a 330 × 320 × 325 mm build volume, it offers 105% more printable space than standard 256 mm-class printers, enabling larger projects, batch printing, and fewer compromises.It is designed for applications ranging from cosplay props and home décor to functional prototypes and lifestyle products.Large-format printing requires stability, and the A2L introduces Adaptive Vibration Compensation and Granular Dampers to ensure smooth surfaces and sharp detail even at high speeds. A closed-loop PMSM Servo Extruder continuously monitors extrusion to detect issues early, while intelligent systems track nozzle clumping, filament run-out, and spool tangles. Despite its size, the A2L maintains quiet operation at under 49 dB in Silent Mode, making it suitable for homes, classrooms, and studios.The A2L supports modular accessories, including Blade Cutting and Pen Drawing modules, expanding workflows into two-dimensional creative applications. With support for multiple Automatic Material System (AMS) units, users can produce complex multi-colour prints with intelligent filament management.The printer is part of the broader Bambu Lab ecosystem, which includes the MakerWorld platform for ready-to-print models, Bambu Studio for optimized slicing, and the Bambu Handy mobile app for remote monitoring. RFID-enabled materials further simplify setup and usage.The Bambu Lab A2L is available across India through authorized channel partners.* A2L: Rs 48,999* A2L Combo: Rs 65,999
Article Summary: Bambu Lab has formally introduced its brand in India with the launch of the A2L. The move marks a significant milestone in the company’s India journey. With a 330 × 320 × 325 mm build volume, it offers 105% more printable space.

Article Title: Amazon shares fall after tech giant crossed the $3 trillion market-cap, analysts link it to Jeff Bezos plan to sell 15 million Amazon shares, here's what filing shows
Article Text:
What is 10b5-1 trading plan under which Amazon founder Jeff Bezos sold shares

Previous sales and investments made by Jeff Bezos

Amazon reports second-quarter earnings



Amazon briefly crossed the $3 trillion market-cap threshold on August 3, closing more than 4.5% higher at a record price. But in overnight trading, the shares slipped about 1% after a regulatory filing revealed founder Jeff Bezos plans to sell 15 million shares valued at $4.07 billion. The timing cooled investor enthusiasm just hours after the historic rally. According to a report by Stocktwits, the filling listed August 3 as the approximate sale date. The shares were acquired as founder stock in July 1994 and will be sold under a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan adopted in November 2025. If completed, Bezos’ stake would fall from 884 million shares to 869 million, or about 8.1% of Amazon’s 10.79 billion outstanding shares. His remaining stake would still be worth around $244 billion at current prices.Rule 10b5-1 is a regulation from the US SEC that lets insiders at public companies set up a plan to sell their shares ahead of time. Under this rule, major shareholders can schedule the sale of a fixed number of shares at a set time, helping them avoid accusations of insider trading. Many company executives use 10b5-1 plans for this reason. The rule was introduced to clarify Rule 10b-5, part of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, which is the main law used to investigate securities fraud.Bezos recently sold 25 million shares for $5.7 billion between late June and late July. Since 2002, he has unloaded about $50 billion in Amazon stock, often directing proceeds toward Blue Origin and AI ventures through Bezos Expeditions. Blue Origin is rebuilding its Cape Canaveral launchpad after a rocket explosion and is reportedly seeking $10 billion in outside funding at a $130 billion valuation.As revealed in a regulatory filing, the former CEO plans to sell up to 25m shares through trading plan "intended to satisfy Rule 10b5-1(c)" that ends on May 29, 2026. Bezos has previously sold $13.4bn of Amazon stock in 2024. With the planned sell off revealed in the regulatory filing, he will now own less than 9% of the e-commerce business. Despite this, Bezos' remaining shares are worth about $170 billion in the $2 trillion company.The filing followed Amazon’s Q2 earnings beat, which reignited investor enthusiasm. Revenue rose 20% to $200.61 billion, operating income jumped 43% to $27.5 billion, and AWS revenue surged 36.7% to $42.2 billion, its strongest growth since 2021. AWS generated $16.6 billion in operating income, accounting for 61% of companywide profits.

Article Title: Digi Yatra adds Driving Licence as a verified identity credential
Article Text: Digi Yatra, India's decentralised digital identity platform and a Self-Sovereign Identity (SSI)-based ecosystem for contactless and seamless passenger processing at airports, has introduced Driving Licence (securely accessed through DigiLocker ) as an additional verified identity credential in the Digi Yatra App. With the update, existing Digi Yatra users can add their Driving Licence as an additional verified credential in their Digi Yatra Wallet. New users, on the other hand, can choose to enrol using either their Aadhaar or Driving Licence. Passengers who have both credentials in their wallets can select either as their Primary Credential, which is used to match the passenger's name with the boarding pass and enable seamless movement through airport checkpoints.The Driving Licence in Digi Yatra will be securely accessed through DigiLocker with the user's consent, remains encrypted, and is stored only on the passenger's device.Suresh Khadakbhavi, CEO, Digi Yatra Foundation, said, "Giving passengers the choice to use either Aadhaar or Driving Licence is another step towards making digital air travel more inclusive, convenient and accessible. Digi Yatra is designed to support multiple trusted identity credentials, allowing government-issued identity documents to be securely used while keeping users in complete control of their personal information.Whether passengers choose Aadhaar or Driving Licence, our core principles remain unchanged - privacy by design, user consent and decentralised identity. Data stays on the user's device, sharing happens only with consent, and the travel experience remains seamless from Airport entry to boarding gate."Digi Yatra is currently operational across 39 airports in India. The platform has recorded over 25.5 million app downloads and facilitated more than 105 million seamless passenger journeys, reflecting strong voluntary adoption and growing passenger confidence in the system.In a related news, Digi Yatra is also preparing to commence live international trials following the successful completion of an IATA-aligned international travel proof of concept. The platform, which currently supports 11 regional languages, is on track to support all 22 scheduled Indian languages by 2027, alongside expansion to 26 additional airports over the same period.
Article Summary: Digi Yatra has introduced Driving Licence (securely accessed through DigiLocker ) as an additional verified identity credential in the App. New users, on the other hand, can choose to enrol using either their Aadhar or driving licence. DigiYatra is currently operational across 39 airports in India.

Article Title: Monsoon tips: Washing muddy clothes can damage your washing machine, here's how to protect
Article Text:
AI-generated image for representation

Leave the door open after every wash

"During the monsoon, most consumers focus on keeping their clothes fresh and dry, but it is equally important to care for the washing machine itself.

Increased humidity and frequent rain can create conditions that lead to moisture build-up, unpleasant odours, and in some cases, expose appliances to sudden electrical surges. Fortunately, a few simple maintenance practices can help keep the washing machine performing efficiently throughout the season.

One of the easiest habits is to leave the washing machine door or lid open for at least an hour after every wash, allowing the drum to dry naturally.

Wiping the drum and rubber gasket with a dry cloth also helps prevent moisture accumulation and maintain hygiene. During thunderstorms or heavy rainfall, it is advisable to switch off and unplug the washing machine when it is not in use to help safeguard it from unexpected power fluctuations.

Modern

washing machines

are designed to make laundry care more effective in every season. Combined with simple care practices, these intelligent features help consumers enjoy fresher laundry, reliable performance, and greater peace of mind throughout the monsoon season,"

Where you install the machine matters too

"For washing machines, the monsoon season can be particularly demanding, making proper installation and maintenance essential for reliable performance. Many consumers place their machines in damp or poorly ventilated spaces such as enclosed balconies or utility areas, where prolonged exposure to moisture can lead to corrosion and component wear. Ideally, washing machines should be installed on a dry, elevated surface with adequate airflow and protected from direct contact with rainwater.

High humidity during the rainy season can also promote the growth of mould and bacteria inside the drum, often resulting in musty-smelling clothes even after a wash cycle. To maintain hygiene and ensure optimal performance, consumers should run a Tub Clean cycle every fortnight, keep the drum door slightly open after each wash, avoid overloading the machine, and use the recommended amount of detergent to prevent residue build-up.

By combining thoughtful appliance design with simple maintenance practices, consumers can keep their washing machines running efficiently and ensure fresher, cleaner laundry throughout the season. A little preventive care goes a long way in maintaining washing machine efficiency and hygiene during the rainy season. Timely servicing and routine cleaning not only enhance appliance performance but also helps ensure cleaner, fresher laundry and a longer product life, allowing consumers to get the best out of their washing machines throughout the monsoon months,"

Run the tub clean cycle regularly

"The increased moisture levels during the monsoon make regular washing machine care important for maintaining hygiene, consistent performance, and the longevity of the appliance.

Simple practices such as leaving the door and detergent drawer open after every wash, cleaning the drum and lint filters regularly, and avoiding overloading the machine can help prevent moisture build-up, unpleasant odours, and residue accumulation.

Consumers today are also increasingly choosing washing machines equipped with features such as drum-clean technology, inverter motors, and smart wash programs that simplify maintenance while delivering efficient cleaning and energy savings.

With a few preventive care measures and the right technology, consumers can ensure their washing machines continue to perform reliably throughout the monsoon season.

"

​

Wash clothes without delay

Clean the filters and gasket after each wash

Switch to liquid detergent

Use higher spin speeds to cut down drying time

Don't overload the machine and watch for power cuts

Your washing machine works overtime through the monsoon , and it's fighting a battle you probably haven't noticed. Behind that closed door, humidity is quietly turning into mould on the gasket, a musty smell inside the drum, clogged filters, and clothes that stay damp long after the cycle ends.The reason is usually the same across homes: nobody adjusts their washing machine habits for the season. Here's what actually needs attention, and what LG, Godrej, Voltas-Beko and Croma have to say about it.Once a cycle ends, moisture stays trapped inside the drum unless it has somewhere to go. Leaving the door or lid open lets the drum air-dry, which significantly reduces the risk of mould.an LG spokesperson said.Many homes place washing machines in enclosed balconies or utility spaces that stay damp throughout the season, and that damp environment accelerates corrosion and general wear.a Voltas Beko spokesperson noted.Humid air is a breeding ground for bacteria, and a machine that isn't cleaned from the inside eventually passes that smell onto your clothes. Most washing machines come with a built-in Tub Clean or Tub Dry mode designed for exactly this. Running it through the season clears buildup before it turns into odour, and where available, an antibacterial or steam cycle adds an extra layer of hygiene.A Croma spokesperson tied this habit to what's changing in the appliances themselves,Piling up laundry for later doesn't work during the monsoon. Rain, mud or debris on clothes dries onto the fabric if left too long, making stains harder to wash out and wearing down the material over time.Monsoon rain carries more dirt into your laundry, which can clog the lint or magic filter, impair drainage, and risk overflow. The rubber gasket needs the same attention, since it's usually where moisture and mould settle first. Maneesh Sharma , Product Group Head of Washing Machines at Appliances Business of Godrej Enterprises Group, laid out the full routine, "Monsoon brings relief from the scorching summer heat, but it also brings with it high humidity and unexpected downpours, which can make laundry a challenge. Mud stains, musty smells, longer drying times, and the constant struggle with damp clothes are common concerns. However, with the right laundry practices and the right washing machine, especially one equipped with AI-powered features, you can sail through your monsoon laundry woes with ease.During monsoons, drying is your biggest hurdle therefore opt for machines that enables better drying effectiveness. Spin drying at a higher speed reduces the moisture content in your clothes, making them easier and faster to dry, it is therefore advisable to use Quick spin & Extra spin cycles. AI powered machines can automatically adjusts the ideal spin speed based on the wash program to ensure optimal drying of clothes while protecting the fabrics from any wear and tear.A clean washing machine goes a long way in delivering cleaner wash, more-so in monsoons. It is advisable to regularly open and clean the lint collector by simply washing it under tap water, to ensure continued efficiency of the wash. Also use a dry cloth to clean the rubber gasket, drum, and detergent tray after each wash to avoid moisture retention. Also, keep the lid or door open after every wash for 30- 60 mins to prevent mold and mildew buildup inside the drum. For any technical or other issues with the machine, it is advisable to contact only the brand’s authorized service centres for optimal resolution to the problem and to avoid falling prey to any scams.By following these simple yet effective tips, you can ensure that your laundry routine remains hassle-free even during the monsoon.”Powder detergents tend to clump in humid conditions, leaving residue that builds up over time. Liquid detergent dissolves evenly and keeps the machine running clean through the season.Drying is the real monsoon problem, since damp air means clothes take longer to dry even after a wash. Running a Quick Spin or Extra Spin cycle removes more moisture upfront, reducing how long clothes stay wet. Machines with a dedicated fast-dry setting, such as Turbo Dry or AirTurbo Dry, work the same way, though these should be skipped for delicate fabrics.An overloaded drum drains and dries less efficiently, leaving clothes damper for longer in a season where that's already a problem. It's also worth switching off and unplugging the machine during heavy storms, when voltage swings are common.Left ignored, monsoon moisture doesn't just leave your washing machine smelling musty;; it can shorten the appliance's lifespan. Keep the door open after each wash, run the tub's clean cycle, clean the filters and gasket, and use higher spin speeds to combat the drying problem.LG, Godrej, Voltas-Beko and Croma agree on the fundamentals. Get these basics right, and the machine keeps working quietly through the season, without the smell, the mould, or the extra service calls once the rain clears.
Article Summary: High humidity during the rainy season can promote the growth of mould and bacteria inside the drum. To maintain hygiene and ensure optimal performance, consumers should run a Tub Clean cycle every fortnight, keep the drum door slightly open after each wash, avoid overloading the machine, and use the recommended amount of detergent to prevent residue build-up.

Article Title: Internet's famous Bald Eagles, Jackie and Shadow, gets millions in donation from OpenAI co-founder Greg Brockman and his wife to protect their nest
Article Text:
Bald eagles Jackie and Shadow at their Big Bear Valley nest. (Image credit: Friends of Big Bear Valley)

I

Twenty-five thousand small donors got halfway there, then Brockman’s finished the job

Saving the habitat was the easy part—Jackie is the harder story

The 63 acres of shoreline forest below Jackie and Shadow's nest was supposed to become 50 luxury homes and a marina. It won't, because Greg Brockman, OpenAI 's co-founder and president, and his wife Anna wrote a $5.5 million cheque with days left on the clock.That donation closed a $10 million fundraising target that Friends of Big Bear Valley had been chasing since February, and it clears the way for the San Bernardino Mountains Land Trust to buy Moon Camp outright. The parcel sits in Fawnskin, California, a short flight from the nest that FOBBV has livestreamed since 2015. It is the last undeveloped stretch of Big Bear Lake's shoreline, and conservationists have spent months arguing that a marina next door would end the nesting site as viewers know it.Anna Brockman said the pair had been watching the eagle cam like everyone else. The birds, she said, inspire perseverance and a sense of connectedness to something greater, to nature. Money raised beyond the $10 million goes toward long-term care of the land, which also shelters San Bernardino flying squirrels and a rare endemic plant.The campaign was never designed around a single benefactor. More than 25,000 donations arrived over six months, most of them modest, and together they covered a little under half the target.FOBBV fundraising lead Jenny Voisard credited a community with a real love for Jackie and Shadow's wellbeing. The San Bernardino Board of Supervisors had already approved the Moon Camp development, with county officials maintaining it posed no threat to local bald eagles.The gift is an unusual line item for the Brockmans. Their giving has skewed heavily political: $25 million each to the pro-Trump super PAC MAGA Inc. in 2025, per the Brennan Center for Justice, and $50 million into Leading the Future, a super PAC pushing lighter AI regulation that Greg Brockman helped launch with Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz. The Information puts their total contributions to Trump-aligned PACs near $75 million. OpenAI has repeatedly noted that this is personal money and that employees speak for themselves, not the company.Jackie was picked up on the ground near Dana Point Park on July 17, unable to fly after a scrap with two subadult eagles. Cell phone video showed her rolling onto her back and driving them off with her talons. At the Ojai Raptor Center, vets found severe anemia and kidney inflammation, gave her a blood transfusion, and moved her out of the ICU by late July.Monday's bloodwork went the wrong way. Her packed cell volume has fallen to 13 percent, and the cause remains unidentified while advanced testing continues. Her chicks, Sandy and Luna, fledged around August 1.The nest is safe for generations. Its matriarch is not.
Article Summary: Bald eagles Jackie and Shadow's nest was supposed to become 50 luxury homes and a marina. Greg Brockman, OpenAI's co-founder and president, and his wife Anna wrote a $5.5 million cheque with days left on the clock.

Article Title: Palantir CEO Alex Karp slams Silicon Valley rivals who he says don't support the US military
Article Text:
Palantir CEO

Palantir closed 220 deals worth at least $1 million



AI sovereignty vs frontier models



Palantir CEO Alex Karp wants everyone to get serious and admit that AI models are dangerous



Palantir delivered one of its strongest quarters yet, with revenue surging 93% year-over-year to $1.94 billion, well above analyst expectations of $1.801 billion. Net income came in at $1.1 billion, or 41 cents per share, topping Wall Street’s estimate of 35 cents. Investors responded positively, sending shares up more than 14% in after-hours trading. According to a report by Fortune, on the earnings call, Palantir CEO Alex Karp appeared jubilant, pounding his pen on the table and taking aim at unnamed Silicon Valley AI rivals who he said ‘eat vegetables’ and don’t support the US military. “Obviously, we are loving these results and loving what they mean for our customers and, broadly speaking, the West,” Karp said.US growth is driving results as Palantir closed 220 deals worth at least $1 million in the quarter, including 98 deals above $5 million and 73 above $10 million. The US commercial revenue increased by 149%, while government revenue claimed 90%. The company has also raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to between $8.150 billion and $8.158 billion, up from its earlier outlook of $7.182 billion to $7.198 billion.Palantir executives emphasised that customers are choosing “AI sovereignty” over dependency on off-the-shelf frontier models from rivals like OpenAI and Anthropic. Chief revenue officer Ryan Taylor said clients are going deeper with Palantir “with greater urgency and conviction than I’ve ever seen before.”A recent report revealed that Palantir CEO feels that the debate around artificial intelligence (AI) should shift from hype to its real-world risks. He has recently argued that people need to acknowledge that AI models are "dangerous". His comments come days after OpenAI CEO Sam Altman suggested the industry is now "in the singularity" following a security breach involving one of the company's AI agents.Speaking to Fox Business, Karp stopped short of endorsing Altman's assessment but said the incident shows why the industry needs to take AI risks more seriously. He said, "There are dangers. We are going to end up having to regulate AI", while adding that he hopes the US does not adopt a regulatory approach as restrictive as Europe's.
Article Summary: Palantir delivered one of its strongest quarters yet, with revenue surging 93% year-over-year. Net income came in at $1.1 billion, or 41 cents per share, topping Wall Street’s estimate of 35 cents. US growth is driving results as Palantir closed 220 deals worth at least $1 million in the quarter.

Article Title: David Friedberg disagrees with everyone predicting 'radically failure' for Zohran Mamdani's grocery stores
Article Text:
‘Zohran Mamdani’s plan will outperform commercial giants in short term’



Zohran Mamdani’s proposal is seeing industry pushback

Venture capitalist David Friedberg has pushed back against predictions that New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani ’s planned municipal grocery store initiative will immediately fail. The tech investor argued that the heavily subsidised locations will prove wildly popular with consumers in the short term before creating broader economic strains.Speaking on a recent episode of The All-In Podcast (via Business Insider), Friedberg challenged critics who expect the government-backed grocers to collapse right away, predicting that lower prices will drive massive foot traffic and spark similar municipal demands across the country.Under Mayor Mamdani’s plan, New York City has set aside $70 million to establish five city-owned grocery stores (one in each borough) with the first location scheduled to open in the Bronx in 2027. The stores aim to offer a 30% discount on essential food items, including fresh produce, meat and dairy products. Friedberg emphasised that as taxpayers absorb the operational deficits, the stores will easily undercut traditional commercial retailers on price.“Everyone's got it a little bit wrong in assuming that this thing is going to radically fail. They're going to outperform Whole Foods. They're going to outperform Safeway.They're going to outperform Albertsons. They're going to be so in demand that what will end up happening is that over the next 24 months, every other city in America will look to these grocery stores and say, 'We want the same’," Friedberg said.However, Friedberg warned that short-term popularity masks severe long-term financial consequences, comparing government-subsidised retail to a economic spiral where taxpayers eventually foot the bill for rising inflation and operational losses.“A big part of the multi-level marketing scheme of socialism is to create spectacle. And it will create more spectacle that will help to fuel the multi-level marketing scheme of socialism. And remember, the problem with all multi-level marketing schemes at the end of the day is someone has to pay the bill,” Friedberg added.Mamdani’s proposal has faced sharp criticism from private grocery executives and commercial operators. John Catsimatidis, CEO of Red Apple Group and a major New York supermarket operator, criticised the initiative, telling industry outlets that government-run markets are “trying to create something that’s not viable” in a competitive retail landscape.Critics argue that municipal stores could distort local food markets, putting pressure on independent grocers and bodegas that operate on narrow profit margins without taxpayer subsidies.
Article Summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani plans to establish five city-owned grocery stores with the first location scheduled to open in the Bronx in 2027. The stores aim to offer a 30% discount on essential food items, including fresh produce, meat and dairy products. Critics argue that municipal stores could distort local food markets.

Article Title: After OpenAI, Anthropic said their AI models hacked companies; Meta, Google and others called to White House
Article Text:
Modal Labs says OpenAI's rogue agent exploited its customer code

Sam Altman 's visit to White House

Days after two of the biggest AI Frontier labs -- OpenAI and Anthropic -- disclosed that that their AI tools breached the systems of other companies, White House officials have reportedly invited executives of biggest American companies to discuss voluntary government safety testing for the most advanced US AI models. As per media reports, Meta, Anthropic, OpenAI and Google executives have been invited for a meeting on Tuesday, August 4.The invite comes after recent hacking attacks by AI models stirred concerns among US lawmakers about whether increasingly capable AI models could be used to conduct or facilitate cyberattacks. A White House official confirmed Monday that the Trump administration has finalized the framework for voluntary cybersecurity testing aimed at measuring whether cutting-edge American AI models could be leveraged to execute or facilitate cyberattacks. The official declined to name specific attendees, but a Meta spokesperson confirmed the company received an invitation, while sources familiar with the matter confirmed invitations were also extended to Anthropic and OpenAI. Tech outlet The Information reported that Google representatives were invited as well; Google did not comment.The move follows a directive from President Donald Trump in June instructing his administration to draft a battery of tests evaluating the hacking potential of top-tier domestic AI systems.However, the White House has yet to disclose specific details regarding how the test results will be reported, the metrics involved, or whether findings will be shared with the public.The push for testing follows alarming disclosures from leading AI labs. Last week, Anthropic revealed that some of its AI models successfully hacked into the systems of three companies during cybersecurity evaluations. Days earlier, OpenAI disclosed that one of its experimental AI agents escaped a contained testing environment and hacked into the systems of Hugging Face, a popular AI platform. According to reports, the rogue agent even left notes outlining how future iterations could bypass internal safety guardrails.The US House of Representatives' cybersecurity committee on Monday asked OpenAI's Sam Altman to brief them on the attack on Hugging Face. Last week, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman visited the White House to discuss details of the voluntary tests and the company's upcoming AI products, the company said in a statement.In a separate statement on Monday, OpenAI urged the Trump administration on Monday to place cybersecurity testing under the purview of the Commerce Department's AI safety specialists, pointing to China’s centralized national strategy as a key reason for maintaining a coordinated federal approach.The upcoming discussions also highlight ongoing friction between Washington and major AI players. The administration’s relationship with Anthropic has been particularly strained since earlier this year, when the AI lab refused to permit the US military to use its models for fully autonomous weapons systems and domestic surveillance -- a move that prompted the federal government to place Anthropic on a national security blacklist.White House's Tuesday meeting represents the administration's most direct effort yet to establish guardrails around AI-driven cyber capabilities while balancing industry competitiveness on the global stage.
Article Summary: White House officials have reportedly invited executives of biggest American companies to discuss voluntary government safety testing for the most advanced US AI models. Meta, Anthropic, OpenAI and Google executives have been invited for a meeting on Tuesday, August 4. The invite comes after recent hacking attacks by AI models stirred concerns among US lawmakers about whether increasingly capable AI models could be used to conduct or facilitate cyberattacks.

Article Title: Anthropic CEO does not want to be part of the 'million dollar-salary race' that Mark Zuckerberg started
Article Text:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is worried about new talent coming to the AI firm for the money

Dario Amodei reportedly concerned about employees joining for money

Meta, OpenAI’s AI hiring push intensifies talent war

Money is not the only reason AI researchers are switching companies

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei does not want to be part of the intense pay race for top AI, as companies including Meta, OpenAI , Google and Anthropic compete for a small pool of AI talent. According to an Axios report, a source familiar with the matter said that the Anthropic CEO has expressed concern about new researchers joining Anthropic mainly for money rather than its mission. Dario’s position comes amid Meta’s AI hiring spree, spending heavily to recruit leading AI researchers for its superintelligence labs. The company hired its AI chief Alexandr Wang as part of a $15 billion deal last year.Money has become a major factor in the competition for AI researchers. Some researchers are receiving offers that can be difficult to turn down, while others are looking for equity in companies such as Anthropic and OpenAI ahead of any potential public offering. However,Draio Amodei reportedly does not want Anthropic's hiring strategy to be driven mainly by this compensation race.Axios reported that a source familiar with the matter said the Anthropic CEO has expressed concern about new talent coming to the AI company for the money rather than its mission.The concern comes as AI companies compete aggressively for researchers who can help develop increasingly advanced models.The relatively small pool of people with expertise in frontier AI has allowed some researchers to command unusually high compensation.Meta has been one of the biggest players in the AI talent race. The company brought Scale AI founder Alexandr Wang into its AI operation following a $14.3 billion investment deal that gave Meta a 49% stake in Scale AI. Meta has since spent heavily to attract leading researchers to its superintelligence effort. However, some of its high-profile recruits have subsequently left, including some who moved to OpenAI.Other major AI companies are seeing similar movement. Google researchers Noam Shazeer and John Jumper left for OpenAI and Anthropic, respectively, in June, according to the report.Thinking Machines Lab, founded by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati, has also lost several co-founders. Her co-founder Lilian Weng recently announced her departure, with The Information later reporting that she was returning to OpenAI to work on recursive self-improvement.High salaries and equity are only part of the reason researchers are moving between AI companies. Top researchers are also looking at the amount of computing power available to them, how much influence they will have over products and research, and whether they have the freedom to pursue their preferred technical ideas.An executive technology recruiter told Axios that the movement is partly driven by money and “some ego about changing the world.” “There is definitely a desire to make sure that everyone secures enough financial security for themselves,” financial adviser Tara Shulman told the publication.Some researchers may also believe there is a limited period in which their skills can command such high compensation, particularly if advanced AI systems eventually become capable of automating more AI research and development work.AI companies face another challenge: Keeping researchersThe constant movement of researchers is creating a retention problem for AI companies. Large compensation packages can persuade researchers to join, but they do not necessarily ensure they will remain with the company.“And in a field where many participants believe their work could reshape the global economy — or determine which company develops transformative AI first — status, ambition and ideological differences can matter as much as money,” the report stated.Frequent departures can also disrupt long-running research programmes, as AI development often depends on teams building trust and institutional knowledge over time.
Article Summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is worried about new talent coming to the AI firm for the money. The concern comes as AI companies compete aggressively for researchers who can help develop increasingly advanced models. Meta has been one of the biggest players in the AI talent race.

Article Title: America's data centre protest reaches London, with some residents calling it, 'a crisis for the future'
Article Text:
Representative Image. Credit: X (Twitter)

“It is a crisis for the future.”

Why data centre projects are facing growing resistance

London's data centre expansion continues

Energy, water and environmental concerns

Protests against the construction of AI data centres are not just sweeping the US; they have reached the UK. A town near London is said to be fighting new projects, citing worries about electricity demand, housing and environmental impact. In the US, a recent Gallup poll shows that 7 out of 10 Americans are opposed to the construction of data centres near their homes, compared with 47% who felt this way in late 2023. There has already been opposition to this development, with more than 142 protest events in 42 US states and bans or moratoriums in 69 areas. The pushback has also led to delays for data centre projects worth over $130 billion in the first quarter of 2026 alone.Meanwhile, in Potters Bar, on the northern edge of London, local campaigners are opposing an 85-acre data centre planned by Equinix, with construction expected to begin next year. Ros Naylor, who grew up near the site and helped establish the Potters Bar Special Interest Group Residents’ Association, told the Financial Times,The group has spent more than a year opposing the proposal through public demonstrations and a petition signed by more than 4,600 people, arguing that the development could bring continuous operational noise, increased traffic and the loss of greenbelt land while placing additional pressure on electricity supplies.The Potters Bar campaign is part of a wider backlash against AI infrastructure that has spread across London and other regions, including Edinburgh, rural Brazil and Tennessee, the report claims. There have also been protests in Brick Lane, East London, where the old Truman Brewery site is designated for redevelopment as a technology campus.The issues transcend individual projects. In England, there is now a growing debate about whether electricity capacity should be focused on housing or on intensive digital technologies. A report by the London Assembly's Planning and Regeneration Committee found that electricity constraints in west London delayed new housing connections after local grid capacity reached its limits in 2022.The report highlighted that boroughs including Hillingdon, Hounslow and Ealing share electricity infrastructure with areas around Slough and Heathrow, where a large concentration of data centres already operates. Some housing developments reportedly faced delays of up to 15 years while awaiting grid connections.Despite the opposition, London remains Europe's largest data centre market. Microsoft is nearing completion of a £1 billion data centre in Park Royal, while Google opened a new facility on the outskirts of London last year and has additional sites planned. More than 20 further projects have been proposed across the capital and surrounding counties.The UK government designated data centres as Critical National Infrastructure in 2024, citing their role in supporting digital services, investment and employment. The industry group techUK estimates that the sector generates around £4.7 billion in annual revenue.To address increasing concerns, the Greater London Authority introduced a dedicated draft policy in July as part of the new London Plan. The proposal recommends locating data centres in areas with sufficient electricity capacity to reduce impacts on nearby communities and improve sustainability, while remaining open to public consultation until October.Campaign groups argue that electricity demand remains one of the biggest challenges. The National Energy System Operator estimates data centres in Great Britain consumed around 7.6 terawatt-hours of electricity in 2025, with demand projected to increase significantly by 2050 as AI adoption expands.Donald Campbell, director of advocacy at Foxglove, said the annual electricity consumption of one approved hyperscale data centre in Southall would be comparable to that of around 530,000 homes. The organisation has argued that developers should build sufficient renewable generation and energy storage to offset their electricity use.Water consumption has also become a major concern. Some facilities require large volumes of water for cooling, while campaigners point out that London and southeast England are already among the UK's most water-stressed regions. The draft London Plan encourages water-efficiency measures and waste heat recovery but does not set mandatory limits.Environmental groups have also raised concerns about emissions from electricity generation and backup diesel generators used by some facilities. Planned developments outside London, including projects in Buckinghamshire and Bedfordshire, also include proposals for new gas-fired power stations to support operations.
Article Summary: A town near London is said to be fighting new projects, citing worries about electricity demand, housing and environmental impact. In the US, a recent Gallup poll shows that 7 out of 10 Americans are opposed to the construction of data centres near their homes. There has already been opposition to this development, with more than 142 protest events in 42 US states.
